nodes.summary: For formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$, the conjunction $\varphi \wedge \psi$ is the formula $\neg(\varphi \to \neg\psi)$.
nodes.title: Conjunction of formulas

nodes.summary: An environment is a map $e : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$ that assigns a real number to each de Bruijn index. For $x \in \mathbb{R}$, the extension of $e$ by $x$ sends index $0$ to $x$ and index $i + 1$ to $e(i)$ for every $i \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Extending an environment

nodes.summary: Given an environment $e : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$, the value of a term in $\mathbb{R}$ is defined by recursion on the term: the variable with de Bruijn index $i$ has value $e(i)$, the integer constant $k$ has value $k$, and the value of a sum, product or negation of terms is the sum, product or negation in $\mathbb{R}$ of the values of its parts.
nodes.title: Evaluation of terms

nodes.summary: For a formula $\varphi$, the formula $\exists \varphi$ is $\neg \forall \neg \varphi$; it binds de Bruijn index $0$ in $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Existential quantification of formulas

nodes.summary: Formulas are built from the atomic formulas $s < t$ and $s = t$, for terms $s$ and $t$, and falsity $\bot$, by implication $\varphi \to \psi$ and universal quantification $\forall \varphi$, which binds de Bruijn index $0$ in $\varphi$. Negation, truth, disjunction, conjunction and existential quantification are defined from these.
nodes.title: Formulas of the language of ordered rings

nodes.summary: For every environment $e : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$, the formula $\exists x.\ x \cdot x = a$ holds under $e$ if and only if the formula $\neg(a < 0)$ holds under $e$. In the first formula the bound variable $x$ is de Bruijn index $0$ and $a$ is index $1$; in the second $a$ is index $0$; in both, $a$ denotes $e(0)$. Thus $e(0)$ is a square in $\mathbb{R}$ exactly when $e(0) \ge 0$.
nodes.title: A real number is a square exactly when it is nonnegative

nodes.summary: Let $\mathrm{qe}$ be the quantifier elimination map on formulas. For every formula $\varphi$ and every environment $e : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$, the formula $\mathrm{qe}(\varphi)$ holds in $\mathbb{R}$ under $e$ if and only if $\varphi$ holds in $\mathbb{R}$ under $e$.
nodes.title: Quantifier elimination preserves truth

nodes.summary: Let $e : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$ be an environment. Whether a formula holds under $e$ is defined by recursion on the formula: $s < t$ holds when the value of $s$ under $e$ is less than the value of $t$ under $e$; $s = t$ holds when these values are equal; $\bot$ never holds; $\varphi \to \psi$ holds when $\varphi$ holding under $e$ implies $\psi$ holding under $e$; and $\forall \varphi$ holds when, for every…
nodes.title: Satisfaction of formulas over the reals

nodes.summary: Let $\mathrm{qe}$ be the quantifier elimination map on formulas. For every formula $\varphi$, the formula $\mathrm{qe}(\varphi)$ is quantifier free.
nodes.title: Quantifier elimination yields quantifier-free formulas

nodes.summary: A formula is quantifier free if it contains no universal quantifier $\forall$.
nodes.title: Quantifier-free formulas

nodes.summary: The negation $\neg\varphi$ of a formula $\varphi$ is the formula $\varphi \to \bot$.
nodes.title: Negation of a formula

nodes.summary: The disjunction $\varphi \lor \psi$ of formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$ is the formula $\neg\varphi \to \psi$.
nodes.title: Disjunction of formulas

nodes.summary: Quantifier elimination is a map sending each formula $\varphi$ of the language of ordered rings to a formula $\operatorname{qe}(\varphi)$, subject to two requirements: $\operatorname{qe}(\varphi)$ is quantifier free, and for every environment $e : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$ assigning a real number to each variable, $\operatorname{qe}(\varphi)$ holds in $\mathbb{R}$ under $e$ if and only if $\varphi$ does.
nodes.title: Quantifier elimination over the reals

nodes.summary: Terms are built from variables $x_i$, one for each natural number $i$ (a de Bruijn index), and integer constants $k \in \mathbb{Z}$, using addition $s + t$, multiplication $s \cdot t$ and negation $-t$.
nodes.title: Terms of the language of ordered rings

nodes.summary: The formula $\top$ is the negation $\neg\bot$ of falsity, that is, the formula $\bot \to \bot$.
nodes.title: The true formula

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
